previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 55-year-old woman was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal pain, consistent with a flare of her chronic gastroparesis. This marked her fourth admission in recent months, with ongoing struggles related to poor oral intake, weight loss, and declining functional status. She presented with tachycardia and dehydration, and labs revealed hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis, both of which improved with IV fluids and electrolyte replacement. Imaging studies, including a chest X-ray and liver ultrasound, showed no acute abnormalities. The patient expressed frustration with her frequent hospitalizations and, for the first time, requested a jejunostomy (J) tube for long-term nutritional support. Surgery agreed she was a candidate but recommended outpatient elective placement after further optimization. Her symptoms resolved during the admission, and she was discharged home with a plan to follow up with surgery and gastroenterology for J tube placement, along with continued management of gastroparesis, osteoporosis, and other chronic conditions.
